conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale** (EPDS). It’s simply a 10-question check-in about how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days, since mood changes are so common after childbirth. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might hurt yourself or someone else, and we’ll take it at your pace so you feel safe and supported. Ready to begin?

First, I’d love to know: over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi, Sarah. I… I can still laugh sometimes, but it feels like I have to work harder to find the funny side than I used to. Like, if my husband makes a joke, I’ll chuckle, but it doesn’t come as naturally as before the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I wouldn’t go that far… I can laugh, but it’s not the same easy, automatic feeling I had before. It takes effort, and sometimes I’m just too tired or preoccupied with the baby to really feel it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some stuff—like when my mom takes the baby for an hour so I can grab a coffee—but the excitement is kind of muted. Before, I’d be counting the minutes; now I’m glad for the break, yet I still feel this little cloud hanging over me, so the enjoyment isn’t as bright as it used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week. When the baby wouldn’t settle at 3 a.m. I kept thinking maybe I’m not feeding him right or I missed some cue, even though everyone says it’s normal. I know in my head it’s not really my fault, but the thought still pops up—like I should be able to “fix” it and I’m failing him.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. Like yesterday the baby sneezed a couple of times and my mind immediately jumped to “What if he’s getting really sick?” I checked his temperature, watched every breath, and couldn’t settle even after my husband told me he was fine. Ten minutes later I realized I’d worked myself up over nothing, but in the moment it feels huge.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panic, but I do get these sudden “what-if” surges—like last night when I was rocking the baby I suddenly pictured myself dropping him or him stopping breathing, and my heart started racing. It passed after a minute, but it left me shaky and on-edge for a while, even though nothing was actually wrong.
Things have been getting on top of me

A bit, yeah. Some days it feels like the dishes, the laundry, the feedings all pile up, and I think, “How am I supposed to keep doing this tomorrow?” I usually get through it, but it’s like I’m constantly playing catch-up and never quite reaching the surface.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. Once I finally get to bed, I mostly sleep okay—it’s just that sometimes it takes me a while to drift off because my mind keeps running through the day or worrying about the next feed. But the sleep itself isn’t broken by feeling unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I do feel that way off and on. It’s not all day, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon when I’m tired and the baby’s fussy—where I just feel heavy and sad, like I’m missing the old ease of things. I usually shake it by evening, but it keeps showing up.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not "so unhappy" exactly… but I did cry twice this week. Once when the baby wouldn’t nap and I felt stuck on the couch for hours, and once when my mom left after helping and the house felt really empty. The tears came more from being overwhelmed than from feeling totally hopeless, and I calmed down pretty quickly both times.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired and low, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Self-report on 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire 3 wks post-delivery.

Areas endorsed above threshold / of clinical note  
• Mood: intermittent sadness, “heaviness,” crying 2× this week; pleasure markedly reduced (laughing/looking forward “muted”)  
• Anxiety: recurrent intrusive “what-if” fears re infant safety, brief adrenergic surges (racing heart, shaky) without clear trigger  
• Guilt/Self-blame: attributes infant fussing to personal failings despite objective reassurance  
• Coping: reports feeling “on catch-up,” easily overwhelmed by daily tasks  
• Sleep: delayed onset due to mental rumination; sleeps once off duty  
• Safety: Denies any self-harm thoughts (Q10)

Summary  
Patient displays sub-syndromal but clinically significant depressive and anxiety symptoms postpartum: anhedonia, tearfulness, excessive guilt, and situational anxiety with mild physiological arousal. No current safety concerns. Findings exceed “baby-blues” expectations at 3 weeks; recommend formal EPDS scoring, follow-up within 1–2 weeks, and psychoeducation on peripartum mood/anxiety disorders.
